purpose: relative-navigation EKF: RMSE, NEES/NIS consistency against declared chi-square intervals, 3-sigma coverage, observability and model-mismatch behaviour, Monte-Carlo with per-cell cluster statistics

setup.truth_models: nonlinear two-spacecraft RK4 (propagate_pair), two-body / J2 / J2+differential-drag (impulsive, BC_dep=0.1, rho0=1.3e-11 kg/m^3, H=50 km); CW family via propagate_cw on the nonlinear chief
setup.assumptions: chief ephemeris exact at every epoch; no measurement latency or drops (E13-03 sensor scope); impulse u=0 every interval; filter Q = 1e-09 m^2/s^3

gates.name: weakly-conditioned range_angle/radial
gates.detail: rank 6 but smin/smax 1.5e-04: full rank only through arc curvature, and the weakest direction is ~1e4 times worse than the best -- the filter sees it as the NEES loss of those cells

gates.name: rank-deficient range_rate/radial
gates.detail: rank 4: range/rate leaves a null space even over the arc -- the RMSE of those cells is the consequence

gates.name: weakly-conditioned range_angle/along_track
gates.detail: rank 6 but smin/smax 3.7e-05: full rank only through arc curvature, and the weakest direction is ~1e4 times worse than the best -- the filter sees it as the NEES loss of those cells

gates.name: rank-deficient range_rate/along_track
gates.detail: rank 4: range/rate leaves a null space even over the arc -- the RMSE of those cells is the consequence

findings: matched CW cell (pos only, radial): position RMSE 0.82 m, NEES pass 0.92 of the chi2(6) 90 % band [1.64, 12.59], NIS pass 0.89, 3-sigma position coverage 1.000 (nominal 0.997) -- the filter is consistent when its model is the truth

measurement combination, matched CW truth, radial: position RMSE 0.72 m (pos+vel) / 0.52 m (range/angle) / 56.01 m (range/rate); NEES pass 0.33 / 0.05 for the two native sets: range+angle pins the LOS polar state but leaves velocity to arc curvature, and range/rate on a short arc is degenerate on the constant-range surface -- the observability ranks below say the same

model mismatch, pos only, radial: CW filter on J2 truth is barely distinguishable from matched -- RMSE 0.82 m, NEES pass 0.83 vs matched 0.92 -- the differential J2 across a 300 m separation is O(1e-6) m/s^2 and the 60 s updates absorb it; the matched nonlinear(+J2) filter sits at 0.77 for the same reason, its extra cost buys nothing at this scale. Drag is the sharp case: CW filter on drag truth -- RMSE 5.14 m, NEES pass 0.14, NIS pass 0.43: the filter reports centimetre covariance while the truth leaves the model, which is exactly the failure NEES/NIS exist to catch

nonlinear(+J2) filter on drag truth: 5.09 m, NEES pass 0.12 -- the nonlinear process model does NOT rescue an unmodelled force: the mismatch is the drag term, not the dynamics approximation. The standard mitigations (drag state in x, or Q inflated to the drag magnitude) are the operational follow-up; the same f(x,u)/Q code path takes them without touching the filter

observability (R-weighted, 20 epochs): pos+vel rank 6/6; range/rate rank 4/6 (smin/smax 0.0e+00 -- a true null space: the along-track/cross-track pair stays unobserved on a 20-minute arc); range+angle rank 6/6 but smin/smax 1.5e-04: full rank only via arc curvature, the weakest direction four decades from the best -- the only sets that are robustly observable are the Cartesian ones and the Cartesian+angle stack

EKF linearisation, matched truth: cells whose update carries angle observables lose consistency at the 30 m initial error (worst NEES pass 0.00, range_angle/along_track) even though RMSE stays < 1 m: the bias is in the linearisation, not the model -- an iterated/UK update is the way back, left to E13-04
